If you already have the code written and deployed and it is just a matter of "not upgrading the backing Ethereum client" then sure. 😄 We have etherchain.org which can follow the PoW chain for a while and beaconcha.in follows the PoS path But if you upgrade your Ethereum client that etherchain is pointing at, they won't see the PoW blocks after the merge. So if you want that, you'll explicitly need to *not* update your clients I believe. right, i think that depends on how the trransition is modelled. If miners receive rewards after merge block +1 , we'd need to have an eye on that Ah, I *think* that idea has been mostly dropped, at least I haven't heard anyone talking about it lately. And if they were rewarded for post-merge mining, I suspect the rewards would be paid out on the post-merge chain, which presumably would surface that data somehow via new APIs. Kind of like how uncles are recorded and published currently, they are just part of a published block in the main chain. ah interesting, how does the post-merge mining work though? Or no concrete ideas yet? None that I have heard. These calls are much more peaceful than ACD calls. 😛 because zoom has different vibes 😄 Probably because I had no mic... Quick call notes: - Explorer may be able to update to updated Eth2 API endpoint to fetch new beacon block contents. Not for first devnet, but later on indexing of post-merge EVM transations in beaconcha.in would be amazing. - Genesis: We embed the deposit contract in genesis state. Pre-fill validator set. Try to keep the eth2 configuration as canonical as possible. We allocate some testnet ether, and can send it to users who want to be on the bleeding edge of first devnet, and help test. - In future testnets we could try make a faucet service - Eth1 follow distance is left unchanged, even though the deposit contract lives on the same chain, since we use the same eth1 voting as the phase0 and merge specs - We use the work-around approach of constant total-difficulty in the first devnet - We will experiment today with genesis configuration and document a devnet setup - No devnet launch date yet. Short-lived and dev-focused at first anyway. Target around first week of hackathon still. Added a description of where consensus messages should be sent from, https://notes.ethereum.org/@n0ble/rayonism-the-merge-spec#Consensus-messages

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content:
Quick call notes:
- Explorer may be able to update to updated Eth2 API endpoint to fetch new beacon block contents. Not for first devnet, but later on indexing of post-merge EVM transations in beaconcha.in would be amazing.
- Genesis: We embed the deposit contract in genesis state. Pre-fill validator set. Try to keep the eth2 configuration as canonical as possible. We allocate some testnet ether, and can send it to users who want to be on the bleeding edge of first devnet, and help test.
- In future testnets we could try make a faucet service
- Eth1 follow distance is left unchanged, even though the deposit contract lives on the same chain, since we use the same eth1 voting as the phase0 and merge specs
- We use the work-around approach of constant total-difficulty in the first devnet
- We will experiment today with genesis configuration and document a devnet setup
- No devnet launch date yet. Short-lived and dev-focused at first anyway. Target around first week of hackathon still.
